DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE

International Trade Administration

[A-570-979]

Crystalline Silicon Photovoltaic Cells, Whether or Not Assembled into Modules, from the
People’s Republic of China: Notice of Court Decision Not in Harmony with the Results of
Antidumping Administrative Review; Notice of Amended Final Results

AGENCY:        Enforcement and Compliance, International Trade Administration, Department of
               Commerce.

SUMMARY: On October 29, 2026, the U.S. Court of International Trade (CIT) issued its final

judgment in Jinko Solar Import and Export Co., Ltd., et. al. v. United States, Consol. Court no.

22-00219, sustaining the U.S. Department of Commerce’s (Commerce) third remand results

pertaining to the administrative review of the antidumping duty (AD) order on crystalline silicon

photovoltaic cells, whether or not assembled into modules, from the People’s Republic of China

covering the period December 1, 2019, through November 30, 2020 (2019-2020 AD

administrative review). Commerce is notifying the public that the CIT’s final judgment is not in

harmony with the final results of the 2019-2020 AD administrative review. Thus, Commerce is

amending the final results of that review by recalculating the dumping margins for Jinko, Risen,

JA Solar Technology Yangzhou Co., Ltd. (JA Solar Yangzhou), Shanghai JA Solar Technology

Co., Ltd. (Shanghai JA Solar), and BYD (Shangluo) Industrial Co., Ltd. (BYD).

DATES: Applicable November 8, 2026

[Contact block omitted.]
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:

Background

[Page 2]
On June 28 and August 10, 2022, Commerce published in the Federal Register the Final

Results and Amended Final Results, respectively, of the 2019-2020 AD administrative review of

crystalline silicon photovoltaic cells, whether or not assembled into modules, (solar cells) from

the People’s Republic of China (China).1 In the Amended Final Results Commerce calculated

weighted-average dumping margins of 20.99 and 12.24 percent for Jinko2 and Risen,3

respectively, and a separate rate of 14.79 percent for JA Solar Yangzhou, Shanghai JA Solar,

BYD, and other non-individually examined companies that qualified for a separate rate

(collectively, the separate rate companies).

        Jinko, Risen, JA Solar Yangzhou, Shanghai JA Solar, BYD, and Trina4 appealed

Commerce’s Amended Final Results. On May 1, 2024, the CIT remanded the Amended Final

Results to Commerce and instructed Commerce to further explain or reconsider the surrogate

values that it assigned to solar glass and air freight, its methodology for calculating facts

available with an adverse inference, and the dumping margin that it applied to JA Solar

Yangzhou, Shanghai JA Solar, and BYD.5

        In its first remand redetermination, issued in August 2024, Commerce explained its

selection of surrogate values for solar glass and air freight and the methodology that it used to

apply facts available with an adverse inference to Risen, and noted that since it made no changes

to its calculations, it was not necessary to recalculate the separate rate assigned to JA Solar

China: Final Results of Antidumping Duty Administrative Review and Final Determination of No Shipments; 2019-
2020, 87 FR 38379 (June 28, 2022) (Final Results); see also Crystalline Silicon Photovoltaic Cells, Whether or Not
Assembled Into Modules, from the People’s Republic of China: Amended Final Results of Antidumping Duty
Administrative Review, 2019-2020, 87 FR 48621 (August 10, 2022) (Amended Final Results).

Jinko Tiansheng Solar Co., Ltd., JinkoSolar (Chuzhou) Co., Ltd., JinkoSolar (Yiwu) Co., Ltd., and JinkoSolar
(Shangrao) Co., Ltd.
3 Risen refers to the collapsed entity comprising Risen Energy Co. Ltd., Risen (Wuhai) New Energy Co., Ltd.,

Zhejiang Twinsel Electronic Technology Co., Ltd., Risen (Luoyang) New Energy Co., Ltd., Jiujiang Shengzhao
Xinye Technology Co., Ltd., Jiujiang Shengzhao Xinye Trade Co., Ltd., Ruichang Branch/Risen Energy
(HongKong) Co., Ltd., Risen Energy (Changzhou) Co., Ltd., and Risen Energy (YIWU) Co., Ltd.
4 Trina refers to the collapsed entity comprising Trina Solar Co., Ltd., Trina Solar (Changzhou) Science and

Technology Co., Ltd., Yancheng Trina Guoneng Photovoltaic Technology Co., Ltd., Changzhou Trina Solar Yabang
Energy Co., Ltd., Turpan Trina Solar Energy Co., Ltd., Hubei Trina Solar Energy Co., Ltd., Trina Solar (Hefei)
Science and Technology Co., Ltd., and Changzhou Trina Hezhong Photoelectric Co., Ltd.
5 See Jinko Solar Import and Export Co., Ltd., et. al., v. United States, 701 F.Supp.3d 1367 (CIT 2024) (Jinko I).

[Page 3]
Yangzhou, Shanghai JA Solar, or BYD.6 The CIT remanded the review to Commerce for a

second time, ordering Commerce to reconsider the surrogate value that it selected for solar glass,

its calculation of facts available with an adverse inference, and its determination of the separate

rate assigned to JA Solar Yangzhou, Shanghai JA Solar, and BYD.7

        In its second remand redetermination, issued in September 2025, Commerce continued to

select the same surrogate value for solar glass, continued to use, and explained why it was

reasonable to use, the same methodology to apply partial adverse facts available (AFA) to Risen,

and continued to assign JA Solar Yangzhou, Shanghai JA Solar, and BYD the same separate rate

that it assigned to these companies in the Amended Final Results.8 The CIT remanded the

review to Commerce for a third time, ordering Commerce to reconsider its valuation of solar

glass and its determination of the separate rate assigned to JA Solar Yangzhou, Shanghai JA

Solar, and BYD.9

        In its final remand redetermination, issued in August 2026, Commerce assigned a new

surrogate value to solar glass and recalculated the separate rate that it assigned to JA Solar

Yangzhou, Shanghai JA Solar, and BYD.10 The CIT sustained Commerce’s final

redetermination.11

Timken Notice

        In its decision in Timken,12 as clarified by Diamond Sawblades,13 the U.S. Court of

Appeals for the Federal Circuit held that, pursuant to section 516A(c) and (e) of the Tariff Act of

at https://access.trade.gov/FinalRemandRedetermination.
7 See Jinko Solar Import and Export Co., Ltd., et. al., v. United States, 789 F.Supp.3d 1275 (CIT 2025).

https://access.trade.gov/FinalRemandRedetermination.
9 See Jinko Solar Import and Export Co., Ltd., et. al., v. United States, 829 F.Supp.3d 1247 (CIT 2026).
10 See Final Results of Redetermination Pursuant to Court Remand, Jinko Solar Import and Export Co., Ltd., et. al.,

v. United States, Consol. Court No. 22-00219, Slip Op. 26-30 (CIT 2026) dated August 13, 2026, available at
https://access.trade.gov/FinalRemandRedetermination.

[Page 4]
1930, as amended (the Act), Commerce must publish a notice of a court decision that is not “in

harmony” with Commerce’s determination and must suspend liquidation of entries pending a

“conclusive” court decision. The CIT’s October 29, 2026, judgment constitutes a final decision

of the CIT that is not in harmony with Commerce’s Final Results (as amended). Thus, this

notice is published in fulfillment of the publication requirements of Timken.

Amended Final Results

        Because there is now a final court judgment regarding the 2019-2020 AD administrative

review of solar cells from China, Commerce is amending its Final Results (as previously

amended) with respect to Jinko, Risen, JA Solar Yangzhou, Shanghai JA Solar, and BYD.

Specifically, in these amended final results of review pursuant to the final court judgement noted

above, Commerce determines that the following estimated weighted-average dumping margins

exist for the companies listed below for the period December 1, 2019, through November 30,

2020:

Cash Deposit Requirements



14 While Risen Energy Co. Ltd. is the only company in this group that was party to the litigation, Commerce treated

Risen Energy Co. Ltd. and the other companies listed here as a single entity in the Final Results and Amended Final
Results. Therefore, the weighted-average dumping margin applies to the entire entity.

[Page 5]
Commerce will issue appropriate cash deposit instructions to U.S. Customs and Border

Protection (CBP) based on these amended results of review. Because Jinko, BYD, JA Solar

Yangzhou, and Shanghai JA Solar each have a superseding cash deposit rate, i.e., Commerce

published in the Federal Register the final results of subsequent reviews covering these

companies, Commerce will not issue revised cash deposit instructions for these companies based

on these amended results of review. Thus, this notice will not affect the current cash deposit

rates for these companies. However, because Risen does not have a superseding cash deposit

rate, Commerce will issue a revised cash deposit instruction regarding Risen to CBP.

Liquidation of Suspended Entries

         At this time, Commerce remains enjoined by the CIT’s order from liquidating entries of

subject merchandise that was exported by Jinko, Risen Energy Co., Ltd., JA Solar Yangzhou,

Shanghai JA Solar, BYD, or Trina15 and entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for

consumption during the period December 1, 2019 through November 30, 2020. These entries

will remain enjoined pursuant to the terms of the injunctions during the pendency of any appeals

process.

         In the event that the CIT’s ruling is not appealed, or, if appealed, upheld by a final and

conclusive court decision, Commerce intends to instruct CBP to assess antidumping duties on

unliquidated entries of subject merchandise exported by Jinko, Risen Energy Co., Ltd., JA Solar

Yangzhou, Shanghai JA Solar, BYD, or Trina in accordance with 19 CFR 351.212(b).

Commerce will instruct CBP to assess antidumping duties on all appropriate entries covered by

this review when the estimated weighted-average dumping margin for the exporter or the

importer-specific ad valorem assessment rate for an importer of the exporter’s subject

merchandise is not zero or de minimis. Where the estimated weighted-average dumping margin


15 In Jinko I, the CIT sustained Commerce’s determination in the Final Results and Amended Final Results that the

collapsed entity comprising the following companies is not eligible for a separate rate: Trina Solar Co., Ltd., Trina
Solar (Changzhou) Science & Technology Co., Ltd., Changzhou Trina Solar Yabang Energy Co., Ltd., Turpan Trina
Solar Energy Co., Ltd., Trina Solar (Hefei) Science & Technology Co., Ltd., and Changzhou Trina Hezhong
Photoelectric Co., Ltd. Therefore, the dumping margin applicable to the Trina single entity is not affected by these
amended results of review and these companies are not listed in the above rate table.

[Page 6]
for the exporter or an importer-specific ad valorem assessment rate for an importer of the

exporter’s subject merchandise is zero or de minimis,16 Commerce will instruct CBP to liquidate

the appropriate entries without regard to antidumping duties.

Notification to Interested Parties

          This notice is issued and published in accordance with sections 516A(c) and (e) and

777(i)(1) of the Act.

Dated: November 6, 2026.

translation_ja:
## 1ページ（対象箇所）

米商務省国際貿易局。案件A-570-979。対象はモジュールに組み込まれているかを問わず、中国産の結晶シリコン太陽電池。米国際貿易裁判所は2026年10月29日、事件22-00219で、2019年12月1日から2020年11月30日までの反ダンピング審査に関する商務省の第3次差戻し結果を支持した。判決と従来の最終結果が一致しないことを通知し、Jinko、Risen、JA Solar揚州、上海JA Solar、BYDのマージンを再計算して結果を改める。文書記載の適用日は2026年11月8日。事前公開日は11月12日、官報掲載予定は11月13日。

## 2ページ（対象箇所）

商務省は2022年6月28日に最終結果、8月10日に修正最終結果を掲載した。修正結果はJinkoが20.99％、Risenが12.24％、独立税率の対象企業が14.79％だった。Jinko、Risen、JA Solar揚州、上海JA Solar、BYD、Trinaが不服を申し立てた。裁判所は2024年5月1日、太陽電池用ガラスと航空輸送の代替評価額、不利な推認を伴う入手可能事実の算定方法、JA Solar揚州、上海JA Solar、BYDへのマージンを説明または再検討するよう命じた。商務省は2024年8月の第1次差戻しで評価額とRisenに用いた方法を説明し、計算を変えず独立税率の再計算を不要とした。脚注1は2022年の最終結果と修正版、脚注2～4は企業群の構成、脚注5は2024年5月1日の判決を指す。

## 3ページ（対象箇所）

裁判所は第2次差戻しで太陽電池用ガラスの代替評価、不利な推認を伴う入手可能事実の計算、独立税率を再検討するよう求めた。商務省は2025年9月の第2次結果で評価額、Risenに用いる方法、JA Solar揚州・上海JA Solar・BYDの独立税率を維持した。裁判所はガラス評価と独立税率を再検討するよう第3次差戻しを命じた。商務省は2026年8月にガラスの評価を変更して独立税率を再計算し、裁判所が支持した。脚注6～11は差戻し結果と裁判所の判断、12と13はTimkenとDiamond Sawbladesを示す。

## 4ページ（対象箇所）

Timken判決とDiamond Sawblades判決に従い、商務省は従来の判断と一致しない裁判所判断を公告し、確定的な判決まで輸入申告の清算を停止する。2026年10月29日の国際貿易裁判所判決についてこの公告を行う。

| 2019年12月1日～2020年11月30日の輸出者 | 加重平均ダンピング・マージン |
|---|---:|
| Jinko企業群（脚注2） | 4.76％ |
| Risen企業群（脚注3、14） | 0.00％ |
| BYD (Shangluo) Industrial Co., Ltd. | 4.76％ |
| JA Solar Technology Yangzhou Co., Ltd. | 4.76％ |
| Shanghai JA Solar Technology Co., Ltd. | 4.76％ |

脚注14。Risen企業群のうちRisen Energyのみが訴訟当事者だった。商務省はグループを単一主体として扱い、マージンは企業群全体に適用する。

## 5ページ（対象箇所）

商務省は米税関・国境警備局（CBP）に現金供託の指示を出す。Jinko、BYD、JA Solar揚州、上海JA Solarには後続審査で設定した現行供託率があるため、今回の修正でこれらの供託率は変わらない。Risenには後続審査による供託率がないため、商務省はRisenについてCBPへ修正指示を出す。裁判所の差止命令により、2019年12月～2020年11月にJinko、Risen Energy、JA Solar揚州、上海JA Solar、BYD、Trinaが輸出した対象品の輸入申告の清算は、上訴手続が続く間も差し止められる。上訴が行われないか確定判決で支持された場合、商務省は19 CFR 351.212(b)に沿って未清算申告の賦課をCBPに指示する方針。脚注15。Trinaの単一主体は独立税率の対象外で今回の修正の影響を受けないため、税率表には載らない。

## 6ページ（対象箇所）

輸出者の推計加重平均マージンまたは輸入者別の従価賦課率がゼロまたは僅少の場合、商務省は対象申告を反ダンピング税を考慮せず清算するようCBPに指示する。僅少の参照規則は19 CFR 351.106(c)(2)。公告の根拠は関税法516A(c)、(e)、777(i)(1)。文書日付は2026年11月6日。
facts_ja: 米商務省は2019年12月～2020年11月の中国製結晶シリコン太陽電池の反ダンピング審査を修正。Jinko 4.76％、Risen 0.00％、BYDとJA Solarの2社は各4.76％。今後の現金供託の改定指示はRisenが対象。
適用日欄は11月8日。11月12日08:45米東部の事前公開、11月13日官報掲載予定。CBPの実際の指示・適用開始と他制度の税負担は未確認。
inference_ja: 対象貨物の資金拘束が減れば調達条件が改善し得る。調達量、CBPの指示、他の税・輸入規制・輸送費が効果を左右する。
missing_parts: 翻訳したページにも未訳の脚注・定型欄または一部段落がある。担当者氏名と連絡先は収録対象外。PDFバイナリは未保存。
参照判決26-133は裁判所PDFの索引本文で結論を照合。直接取得は404で原本、目視、日本語訳は未収録。

        In its second remand redetermination, issued in September 2025, Commerce continued to

reasonable to use, the same methodology to apply partial adverse facts available (AFA) to Risen,

and continued to assign JA Solar Yangzhou, Shanghai JA Solar, and BYD the same separate rate

that it assigned to these companies in the Amended Final Results.8 The CIT remanded the

review to Commerce for a third time, ordering Commerce to reconsider its valuation of solar

glass and its determination of the separate rate assigned to JA Solar Yangzhou, Shanghai JA

Solar, and BYD.9

        In its final remand redetermination, issued in August 2026, Commerce assigned a new

surrogate value to solar glass and recalculated the separate rate that it assigned to JA Solar

Yangzhou, Shanghai JA Solar, and BYD.10 The CIT sustained Commerce’s final

redetermination.11

Commerce will issue appropriate cash deposit instructions to U.S. Customs and Border

Protection (CBP) based on these amended results of review. Because Jinko, BYD, JA Solar

Yangzhou, and Shanghai JA Solar each have a superseding cash deposit rate, i.e., Commerce

published in the Federal Register the final results of subsequent reviews covering these

companies, Commerce will not issue revised cash deposit instructions for these companies based

on these amended results of review. Thus, this notice will not affect the current cash deposit

rates for these companies. However, because Risen does not have a superseding cash deposit

rate, Commerce will issue a revised cash deposit instruction regarding Risen to CBP.

Liquidation of Suspended Entries

         At this time, Commerce remains enjoined by the CIT’s order from liquidating entries of

subject merchandise that was exported by Jinko, Risen Energy Co., Ltd., JA Solar Yangzhou,

Shanghai JA Solar, BYD, or Trina15 and entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for

consumption during the period December 1, 2019 through November 30, 2020. These entries

will remain enjoined pursuant to the terms of the injunctions during the pendency of any appeals

process.

         In the event that the CIT’s ruling is not appealed, or, if appealed, upheld by a final and

conclusive court decision, Commerce intends to instruct CBP to assess antidumping duties on

unliquidated entries of subject merchandise exported by Jinko, Risen Energy Co., Ltd., JA Solar

Yangzhou, Shanghai JA Solar, BYD, or Trina in accordance with 19 CFR 351.212(b).

Commerce will instruct CBP to assess antidumping duties on all appropriate entries covered by

this review when the estimated weighted-average dumping margin for the exporter or the

importer-specific ad valorem assessment rate for an importer of the exporter’s subject

merchandise is not zero or de minimis. Where the estimated weighted-average dumping margin
